sys.cubic.rule: 3 equal axes, all at 90° (a = b = c)
sys.tetragonal.rule: 2 equal axes and a different c axis, all at 90° (a = b ≠ c)
sys.orthorhombic.rule: 3 unequal axes, all at 90° (a ≠ b ≠ c)
sys.hexagonal.rule: 3 equal axes at 120° in one plane (a₁, a₂, a₃) and a perpendicular c axis
sys.trigonal.rule: Like hexagonal: 3 axes at 120° and a c axis, with 3-fold symmetry
sys.monoclinic.rule: 3 unequal axes, only one angle different from 90° (β)
sys.amorphous.rule: No crystal structure: no axes to draw
sys.organic.rule: Produced by a living being: no crystal system to draw

les.anim.t.edge: The shadow edge seen in the eyepiece
les.anim.t.liquid: With and without a drop of contact liquid
les.anim.with: With liquid: the light gets through
les.anim.without: Without liquid: total reflection on the air

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.desc: Which personal data is collected, why, for how long, and how to exercise your rights.
privacy.intro: This page explains which personal data {site} collects, why, how long it is kept, and how to exercise your rights (General Data Protection Regulation, GDPR). Reading the site, the encyclopedia and the lessons does not require an account.
privacy.s1.h: Who is responsible for your data
privacy.s1.p:
The data controller is {name}, {address}.
For any question about your data: {email}.
privacy.s2.p:
• When you create an account: your e-mail address, your username and your password. The password is never kept in clear text: only an irreversible fingerprint is stored.
• When you use the site: your forum messages and reports, and your quiz results.

For security, your IP address and your e-mail address are counted for two days at most in order to limit abuse (too many login attempts or messages), then these counters are deleted. The host may also keep technical connection logs, for the period required by law.
privacy.s3.p:
• To create and manage your account, give you access to the simulator and the forum, and keep your progress in the quizzes: performance of the service you ask for.
• To send the essential e-mails (address confirmation, forgotten password): performance of the service.
• To protect the site against spam and abuse, and to moderate the forum: legitimate interest of the publisher.

{site} does not sell your data and does not use it for profiling.
privacy.s5.p: Your data is kept as long as your account exists. You can delete it at any time from the My account page: your e-mail address, username, password, sessions and quiz results are then erased. The messages you wrote on the forum stay displayed under a neutral name (“membre-supprime”), so that the discussions still make sense; you can ask for them to be deleted in writing through the Contact page. If you add a gemstone price it is kept without any seller name; when your account is deleted it stays in the price table, made anonymous.
privacy.s6.p: Your data is only accessible to the publisher and, for technical operation, to the host ({host_name}) and to the e-mail sending service used. It is not sold. The forum is reserved for members: your messages and your username are visible there to the other members.
privacy.s7.p: You can at any time access your data, have it corrected, have it erased, limit its processing, object to it and retrieve it. To do so, write to {email}; the account can also be deleted by yourself from the My account page. You get an answer within one month.
privacy.s8.p: If you believe, after contacting us, that your rights are not respected, you can lodge a complaint with the French data protection authority, the Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés (CNIL), www.cnil.fr.
privacy.s9.p: This policy may change, for example if a new function collects new data. The date of the last update is shown at the bottom of the page.

fig.desc.criteria: A gem in the centre, linked by five lines to the five qualities: beauty, rarity, durability, value and acceptability. The quality studied in this step is highlighted.
fig.desc.taxonomy: The family tree of gems: natural gems (crystalline, or non-crystalline: amorphous and organic) and non-natural gems (synthetic, with no natural counterpart, assembled), with examples.
fig.desc.hardness: The Mohs scale as ten bars of growing height, from talc to diamond; depending on the step, the absolute hardness, a point that scratches a stone or not, or the hardness pencils drawn one by one across the stone.
fig.desc.interf: The interference figures seen in the conoscope: a black cross surrounded by coloured rings for a uniaxial stone, a pale round spot in the centre for quartz, two “eyes” and a “moustache” for a biaxial stone.
fig.desc.spectro: The spectrum of white light split by a prism, from 400 nm (violet) to 700 nm (red), then the dark absorption lines and bands of a few stones: ruby, emerald, peridot, almandine garnet.
fig.desc.chelsea: The two windows of the Chelsea filter (yellow-green and deep red), then stones seen with the naked eye and through the filter: chromium and cobalt turn red, iron does not.
fig.desc.uv: The scale of light with the two ultraviolet lamps (254 nm and 365 nm), a stone that absorbs UV and glows, two sapphires with different reactions, then fluorescence that stops and phosphorescence that lasts.
fig.desc.dichro: A coloured stone whose colour changes when it is turned, seen through the two halves A and B of the London dichroscope, then examples: isotropic, uniaxial, biaxial.
fig.desc.tenacity: A hammer hits a stone: it splits along a smooth plane (cleavage), breaks irregularly (fracture) or takes the blow; a scale of toughness, from poor to exceptional.
fig.desc.stability: A stone exposed to light, heat or chemicals: its colour fades, it cracks or its surface is attacked.
fig.desc.loupe: A dirty stone with a whitish film, wiped with the chamois; then the stone turned in all directions, and seen through the 10× loupe.
fig.desc.carat: A two-pan balance: a carob seed against a one-carat stone (1 ct = 0.2 g), then the weight of a stone shown in carats and in grams.
fig.desc.hydro: A stone hanging from the balance, first in air then dipped in water, with the two weights displayed and the density formula.
fig.desc.systems: A crystal in perspective turning around, with its axes a, b and c (or a₁, a₂, a₃ and c for hexagonal), for each of the seven crystal systems; then the growth shapes (needle, prism, plate) and the three optical families.
fig.desc.polariscope: A lamp, a polarizer, a turning stone, an analyzer and the eye: between crossed filters, an isotropic stone stays dark, an anisotropic stone lights up four times per turn and an aggregate stays bright; then the conoscope figures.

price.title: Estimate the price of a gemstone
price.desc: A price range for a coloured gemstone, based on prices recorded by members: species, weight, colour, clarity, treatment.
price.lead: Pick a species and a weight: the site gives a range, computed only from real, checked prices, without naming any seller. If there are too few prices, it says so.
price.disclaimer.title: Please read first.
price.disclaimer.text: This figure is a guide only: it is not an appraisal, an official valuation or buying or selling advice. Two stones of the same species, weight and colour can be worth very different amounts (cut, origin, certificate, market conditions).
price.pick: Choose a species and a weight between 0.05 and 500 carats.
price.none: No price is recorded yet for this species with these criteria. No estimate is given rather than an invented figure.
price.few: Only {n} price(s) recorded with these criteria: at least {nmin} close to this weight are needed for an honest range. Try widening the criteria (colour, clarity, treatment) or add a price you have seen.
price.result.title: {species}, {weight} ct
price.result.ppc: That is {low} to {high} € per carat (central value {median} €).
price.result.n: Based on {n} prices ({asking} asking, {paid} paid), the most recent from {date}. Only prices from the last {months} months count.
price.method.band: Method: prices of stones from {lo} to {hi} ct ({n} prices). The range goes from the lower to the upper quarter of these prices.
price.method.trend: Method: trend between weight and price per carat, drawn from all the prices (too few prices in this weight band). Less reliable.
price.conf.high: Confidence: good (many prices in this band).
price.conf.low: Confidence: low, take it as an order of magnitude.
price.bands.title: Prices by weight band
price.chart.label: Chart: price per carat of the recorded stones by weight, with the estimated range.
price.chart.legend: Each dot is a recorded price (filled dot: asking price, hollow dot: price paid). The vertical line is the weight you asked for, the dot at its centre the central value and the segment the range.
price.invite: Add a price I have seen
price.top.title: Species with the most prices
price.top.empty: The price table is just starting: no price is published yet. Members can add the prices they come across, and they appear here after checking.
price.how.title: How is the range calculated?
price.how.p1: The site groups the checked prices of the species by weight band, drops the extreme values, then gives the median and the zone holding half of the prices. With too few prices in the band it gives nothing or, if there are enough overall, a less reliable trend.
price.how.p2: Prices come from members and from files imported by the administrator, never with a seller's name. An asking price is a listed price, often negotiable; a price paid is that of a completed sale. Prices older than 24 months are ignored.
price.add.title: Add a price you have seen
price.add.lead: Have you seen or paid for a stone? Give its price: it will be checked, then used to improve the estimates.
price.add.rules: Do not give a seller's name, a website address or a certificate number. Only real prices are accepted; invented or repeated prices are rejected.
price.add.color.help: Pale: light tone. Medium: a clear colour. Vivid: strongly saturated, like the fine stones on the market. Exceptional: the top of the species.
price.add.confirm: I confirm that this price is real and that I recorded it myself.
price.err.species: Choose a species from the list.
price.err.weight: The weight must be between 0.05 and 500 carats.
price.err.price: The price must be between 1 and 2,000,000 €.
price.err.ppc: This price per carat is not credible: check the weight and the price.
price.err.choice: One of the lists (type of price, colour, clarity, treatment) is not filled in.
price.err.month: The month must be one of the last 24 months, not in the future.
price.err.confirm: Tick the box to confirm that the price is real.
